behavior.verify: Test: the area carries no aria-haspopup, aria-expanded or aria-controls, open or closed, and keeps a product's own; the open menu has the menu role, no aria-labelledby, and the product's aria-label where it gives one; axe finds no violation.

behavior.text: THE menu SHALL draw the rows of every surface at its density. WHILE density is regular each row SHALL take the regular value of every token of the density axis this spec names (comp.menu.container.height.regular, comp.menu.container.padding-block.regular, comp.menu.container.padding-inline.regular, comp.menu.container.gap.regular, comp.menu.leading-icon.size.regular, comp.menu.trailing-icon.size.regular, comp.menu.mark.size.regular, comp.menu.group-title.padding-inline.regular); WHILE density is compact it SHALL take the compact value of each in its place (comp.menu.container.height.compact, comp.menu.container.padding-block.compact, comp.menu.container.padding-inline.compact, comp.menu.container.gap.compact, comp.menu.leading-icon.size.compact, comp.menu.trailing-icon.size.compact, comp.menu.mark.size.compact, comp.menu.group-title.padding-inline.compact), so that a compact row is lower, set in less from its edges and draws smaller glyphs, the room a row keeps for an empty column (MNU-59) shrinking with them. The text styles, the surface and its paddings, the dividers, the group gap and the control of a checkbox or radio item SHALL be the same in both. Every submenu SHALL take the menu's density. WHEN density names a value the active design system does not have THE menu SHALL draw the default density's rows and in debug builds report the unknown value; a density a design system added SHALL be drawn from that density's tokens, as the core values are. WHEN density changes while the menu is open THE menu SHALL draw the new rows at once, without a motion, keeping focus where it is.
behavior.verify: Fixture density-compact under the default system: with a mouse every row is 32 high, its glyphs 20, its content 8 from the row's edges; under touch emulation every row is 48. Its labels are drawn in the regular rows' text style.

behavior.text: WHEN the element the open menu is placed against — the anchor; for a context menu its area, or the element a keyboard request was made on (MNU-61) — is no longer drawn: taken out of the page, given no box (on the web display none on it or on an ancestor), made invisible (visibility hidden) or skipped by its platform's content visibility (on the web content-visibility hidden, or auto while it is off screen), THE menu SHALL emit close once with the reason anchor-hidden and be closed as MNU-5 says, every open submenu with it (MNU-49), and SHALL NOT place its surface against that element while it is not drawn, because a surface with nothing beside it no longer says what it belongs to. WHEN it closes with focus inside it THE menu SHALL return focus as MNU-49 says and, where that element cannot take focus, SHALL NOT keep focus inside its closed surfaces. WHEN the element is drawn again while the menu is still open THE menu SHALL follow it again, and emit close again the next time it is no longer drawn.
behavior.verify: Test: an open menu with a submenu open, opened from the keyboard, whose anchor is given display none, is taken out of the page, is inside a box given content-visibility hidden, and is given visibility hidden, emits close once each time with the reason anchor-hidden, closes the submenu with it and leaves focus outside the menu; the anchor drawn again, the menu opens beside it and follows it.

behavior.text: WHERE the platform has ARIA attributes (the web), WHILE an item is a link item its role is carried by its anchor (MNU-53), and WHEN the product sets an aria- attribute on its host, by the attribute or by the ARIA property that reflects it, THE menu SHALL move it to the data-aria- attribute of the same name, so that the host is no second node with its name, description or state, and SHALL expose it on that anchor — an id reference by the elements it names in the host's tree or a tree around it, a description after its own — except those the item owns (aria-disabled, aria-current, aria-keyshortcuts), which it SHALL move, not expose and report in debug builds; its label is its name over a name given so, and while label is empty a name given so is its name. WHEN the item stops being a link item THE menu SHALL give back to its host what it moved, as it was written, and WHEN it becomes one SHALL move what the host carries. WHEN the product removes one, or its data-aria- twin, or sets the ARIA property that reflects it (ariaLabel, ariaDescribedByElements…) to null, THE menu SHALL take it off the anchor.

WHERE the platform has ARIA attributes (the web), the hosts of the menu, of an item that is not a link item (a checkbox item, a radio item and a submenu item included) and of a group carry their roles themselves (MNU-24), so what the product writes on them is not moved, but for a name: WHILE an item's or a group's label, or the anchor that names a menu, is not empty THE menu SHALL hold the product's aria-label and aria-labelledby on that host as their data-aria- twins, so that its own is the whole name although the platform gives aria-labelledby the precedence, and WHEN it is emptied SHALL give them back as they were written; WHILE it is empty a name the product gives so is the name and an item SHALL NOT be reported as having none in debug builds (MNU-26) — a context menu is named so (MNU-63). WHILE a menu is closed, or a group is in a group (MNU-29), it exposes nothing, and THE menu SHALL hold them as well, giving them back when it is exposed again. WHEN the product removes one, or its data-aria- twin, or sets the ARIA property that reflects it to null, THE menu SHALL take it away.

keyboard.action: The product opens the menu; focus moves to the first enabled item.

keyboard.keys: Shift+F10 or the ContextMenu key on the area or an element inside it (trigger context)
keyboard.action: The menu asks to be opened against that element (contextRequest); the product opens it, and focus moves to the first enabled item.
Moves focus to the next or previous item of the level that holds focus, wrapping at the ends.
Moves focus to the first or last item of that level.
Moves focus to the next item of that level whose label begins with the characters typed.

keyboard.keys: Right Arrow (Left Arrow in a right-to-left layout) on a submenu item

keyboard.keys: Left Arrow (Right Arrow in a right-to-left layout) in a submenu
keyboard.action: Closes that submenu and returns focus to its submenu item.
Activates the focused item and closes the menu and its submenus, a link item's destination opening after that; on a submenu item, opens the submenu instead.

keyboard.keys: Enter with a modifier key, on a link item (the web)
keyboard.action: What the browser does with a link: another tab or window, a download. The menu emits no close and stays open, with focus on the item (MNU-54).

Closes the innermost open submenu and returns focus to its submenu item; with no submenu open, closes the menu and returns focus to the anchor (a context menu: to the element that had focus when it was asked for).
Closes the menu and every submenu, and moves focus on from the anchor.

accessibility.labeling: The menu is named by its anchor (a context menu by the name the product gives it, and by none where it gives none), and a submenu by its submenu item's label. Each item's label is its name and its supporting text its description; its shortcut is exposed as the item's keyboard shortcut where the platform has one, and otherwise given as text in its description (KBS-10); trailing text is description only. A link item is a menu item like any other, named by its label; while it opens a new context its targetLabel ends its description. Checkbox and radio items expose their checked state, whatever their mark looks like. A submenu item exposes that it opens a menu and whether that menu is open. A group is named by its title. Icons, the mark and the submenu indicator are decorative.
notes: The anchor is the product's own button, icon-only Button or field. The menu does not draw it; it reads its position, returns focus to it, and sets its expanded state where the platform has one (aria-haspopup and aria-expanded on the web).

A context menu (trigger context) is the same menu opened at a point of an area instead of from a button: a secondary click, a long press, Shift+F10 or the ContextMenu key, as the WAI-ARIA menu pattern names for a context-specific menu. The area is not a button, so it carries no popup state; the menu cancels the platform's own context menu only where it answers the request, and a product that cancels contextRequest — over a field, a link, selected text it does not handle — leaves the platform's menu in place. Every action a context menu offers is also reachable elsewhere in the product, because a context menu is found only by those who know to ask for it (MNU-60 to MNU-63).

Five item kinds: item (an action), checkbox-item, radio-item, submenu and group. A checkbox item's checked is its own; which radio item is checked is its group's, by value; a submenu item's open is its own. A group may hold items of any kind except another group; a submenu may hold items of every kind.

A link item is the platform's own link exposed as a menu item: on the web an anchor with the menu item role. Assistive technology reads a menu by its items — how many, which one, the arrow keys — and that reading holds only while every child of the menu is a menu item; so the role stays, and what makes the row a link stays underneath it: its address, the browser's context menu and new-tab gestures, a crawler that follows it. It is the one link form that Space activates, because it is operated as a menu item and looks like the action beside it. A menu of nothing but links to a site's main pages, always in view, is navigation and belongs in a navigation landmark of links; the menu is for a short set that is out of the way until asked for (the folded levels of a trail, a choice of language, "more").

Focus: the menu is an operated overlay that is not modal. It moves focus in when it opens and returns it to the anchor when it closes, but does not keep it: Tab leaves the menu and closes it, at whatever level focus is. A submenu takes focus when it is opened by a key or a press and returns it to its submenu item when it closes alone.

Submenus follow the WAI-ARIA menu pattern: the arrow key that points to where the submenu opens, Enter and Space open it and move focus in; the opposite arrow key and Escape close it and return focus to its item; type-ahead, Home, End and the vertical arrow keys work inside the level that holds focus. A pointer opens a submenu by resting on its item, and may then cross other items on its way to the submenu without closing it (MNU-45); touch opens it with a tap. In a window too narrow to set two surfaces side by side the submenu is laid over its parent, never swapped in for it, so the keys, the roles and the reading order are the same at every size (MNU-47).

Depth: one level of submenus where possible, never more than two. Each level costs a person a precise sideways movement and hides the level before it on a small screen; a set that needs more belongs in a dialog, a sheet or a page. A debug build reports a third level; nothing stops it from working (MNU-52).

A checked item is told from an unchecked one by its mark, which differs in shape (an empty and a filled box, a thin and a heavy ring, a check or none), never by the row's fill alone: the fill supports the mark and is not held to a contrast of its own. It is still meant to be seen: in the default system a checked row's fill is a layer of the row's content color over the sheet, so it differs from the sheet and from a hovered row by the same step in every scheme (MNU-37), and the content on it keeps at least 4.5:1 in every state. The control looks are drawings in the mark column; the menu holds no checkbox and no radio button.
Under gap no separator is exposed between groups; the groups themselves, and their titles, carry the structure to assistive technology, as they do under divider.
A menu holds only its items. A field, slider or switch inside a menu would take arrow keys and typing that the menu needs.
Text size does not clip an item: items grow at 200% text size, and the surface scrolls when it no longer fits the visible part of the window.

An item's shortcut is drawn by the keyboard shortcut component (KBS-13), which writes the keys for the keyboard the person uses and only shows them: the product binds them. Trailing text is never read as a shortcut; a product that typed its shortcut there keeps the text but not the keyboard shortcut semantics until it moves the keys to shortcut.
How a state looks is a value decision of the active design system; components read the state's tokens and never compute the effect themselves.

WCAG 2.5.8 (target size): for touch every row is at least the touch target high in both densities (MNU-12). The compact density is lower than the pointer target for a fine pointer, by design: it is the density of a tool used with a mouse, it stays above the 24 by 24 the criterion asks, and its rows reach across the surface's whole width. A product that cannot accept that uses regular.

item.name: tanrei-menu-item
item.notes: With `href` the item's shadow root holds an `<a role="menuitem" tabindex="-1">` in place of its row element, drawn through the shared link primitive (`packages/web/src/primitives/link.ts`) as `<tanrei-list-item>`'s is, with Space left among the keys that press it (MNU-54). `target` is the `target` attribute with the values `same` and `new` (the HTML spellings `_self` and `_blank` are read as those two), `targetLabel` the `target-label` attribute, and `rel` (to which `new` adds `noopener`) and `download` are web-only and forwarded to the anchor. `click` is the anchor's own click: cancelling it (`preventDefault()`) cancels the navigation and not the menu's `close`. The menu fires `close` from that click only when `event.button` is 0 and no modifier key is down; Enter with a modifier key is passed to the anchor, and Space calls the anchor's `click()`. A disabled link item is the anchor without `href`, with `aria-disabled="true"`. An `href` attribute on `tanrei-menu-checkbox-item`, `tanrei-menu-radio-item` or `tanrei-submenu` is ignored and reported (MNU-57).

submenu.name: tanrei-submenu
submenu.notes: `<tanrei-submenu label="Open recent">` holds the submenu's items as its children, as `tanrei-menu` holds its own; it draws the row in its parent's surface and its own surface as a manual popover in the top layer. `open` reflects, and `toggle` fires on it and bubbles.

group.name: tanrei-menu-group
group.notes: The title is the `label` attribute, as `<optgroup label>`: a `title` attribute would also draw the browser's tooltip. The group sets its own `value` before firing `change`.

web.notes: `tanrei-menu` (open, placement, separation, and `anchor`: the id of the anchor element, as the HTML anchor attribute) holds `tanrei-menu-item`, `tanrei-menu-checkbox-item`, `tanrei-menu-radio-item`, `tanrei-submenu` and `tanrei-menu-group` children; item attributes are kebab-case (`supporting-text`, `leading-icon`, `trailing-icon`, `trailing-text`, `mark-icon`). `click`, `change` and `toggle` fire on the item or group and bubble, so one listener on the menu can take them all. The surface is a manual popover in the top layer, placed with CSS anchor positioning and a script fallback where the browser has none; each submenu's surface is a popover of its own, placed against its `tanrei-submenu` the same way. The menu implements its own light dismiss so that it can emit `close` with a reason, and treats every surface of its tree as inside. A press outside also reaches the element under it. It sets `aria-haspopup="menu"`, `aria-controls` and `aria-expanded` on the anchor element, and the same three on each submenu item's row. The `inline` attribute, for tests, draws the open surface in place, with each open submenu beside it (MNU-19). The mark is the `mark` part: the box or the ring of a control look, drawn by the menu's own styles from `--tanrei-comp-menu-control-*`, or the icon helper's glyph (MNU-22, MNU-38). The submenu indicator is the icon helper's `chevron_right` in the `submenu-indicator` part. A group's title is inset by `--tanrei-comp-menu-group-title-padding-inline-regular` from the rows' edges (MNU-28). The link item is not built on this platform yet: MNU-53 to MNU-57 and what MNU-6, MNU-19 and MNU-24 say of it, with the fixtures links, links-rtl and links-trailing. A link item's `current` writes `aria-current="page"` on its anchor and draws the row from the current condition (MNU-58). Under gap each group, and each run of items outside a group, is a `.tile` (part `tile`) of its own inside the scroll box; under divider the tiles are boxes with no look (MNU-36). `trigger` is the `trigger` attribute; with `context`, `anchor` names the area. `contextRequest` is `contextrequest`, a cancelable event whose `detail` is `{ x, y, element, input }`: client coordinates, the element under the pointer or with focus, and `pointer`, `long-press` or `keyboard`. The menu listens on the area for `contextmenu` (a secondary click, Android's long press, the context-menu command of assistive technology) and cancels it unless the product cancels the request; for a touch or a pen held still, which WebKit on iOS answers with no `contextmenu`; and for Shift+F10 and the ContextMenu key on `keydown`, whose own `contextmenu` it then cancels. After a long press the release of that press, and its click, go no further. On iOS a long press may also select text: an area whose text is not to be selected says so in its own styles (`user-select`, `-webkit-touch-callout`).

group.name: TanreiMenuSection
group.notes: `TanreiMenuSection(_ title:) { … }` as `Section`; `TanreiMenuSection(_ title:, selection:) { TanreiMenuOption … }` for radio items, as an inline `Picker`. Writing the binding is change.

swiftui.notes: A modifier on the anchor, `.tanreiMenu(isPresented:placement:) { … }`, as `.popover`, presented with `presentationCompactAdaptation(.popover)` so it stays a popover on iPhone; a press outside does not reach what is under it. The content builder takes the item views. `disabled` follows `.disabled(_:)`. Closing writes `false` to `isPresented`, which is close. SwiftUI's own `Menu` is not used: its items cannot be tokenised. Ships the previous revision today (the check stroked as a path in a 16 box, a group's title starting where the labels start). Not built on this platform yet, among the rest of this spec: the submenu item kind and everything about it (MNU-42 to MNU-52), `separation` (MNU-35, MNU-36), the checkbox and radio looks of the mark and `markIcon` (MNU-38 to MNU-41) and their 17 fixtures; the selected fill and colors arrive through the tokens, the fill of a checked row with them: none at standard contrast in the default system, as MNU-37 says. Reading comp.menu.separation, comp.menu.checkbox-item.mark and comp.menu.radio-item.mark as typed choices needs this platform's token output to write a component's choice as a typed enumeration, which it does not yet. Nor is the link item: MNU-53 to MNU-57 and what MNU-6, MNU-19 and MNU-24 say of it, with the fixtures links, links-rtl and links-trailing. Lagging behind MNU-58 (a link item's current, drawn with the selected fill) and MNU-36 (the groups as separate tiles under gap): it has neither yet. Not built yet: iconSpace (MNU-59) — this platform still keeps the mark and leading icon columns in every row of a surface where any item draws in them. Not built yet: the context trigger (MNU-60 to MNU-63) — this platform opens the menu from an anchor only.

item.name: MenuItem

An `href` on an entry of another kind is ignored and reported (MNU-57).
